label: prf:brings-is-qou
title: Proof of Bring's surface is a quantum observable universe
html:
Item (1). The quantised coordinate ring A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is a Hopf algebra over R[q, q^{-1}] with antipode S, counit \varepsilon, and the Haar state h_q \colon A \to R furnishing a non-degenerate Frobenius form \int_A = h_q (non-degeneracy follows from the faithfulness of the Haar state for compact quantum groups). The category \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) is R-linear, rigid monoidal (duals given by contragredient representations), and the forgetful functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod} is exact, faithful, and monoidal. The Woronowicz left-covariant 3D differential calculus [woronowicz1987-twisted-su2] \Omega^1(A) = \ker(\varepsilon) / \ker(\varepsilon)^2 is a 3-dimensional A-bimodule in \mathbf{C}, providing the differential calculus axiom; we use the left-covariant (not bi-covariant) 3D calculus of [woronowicz1987-twisted-su2] throughout.

Item (2). The adjoint representation \mathrm{Ad}(A) decomposes under \mathrm{SU}_q(2) into irreducible representations of spin j \geq 1 (the spin-0 component vanishes because \mathrm{Ad} \cong V_1 \oplus V_2 \oplus \cdots with no trivial summand). Therefore \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 by the quantum Schur lemma.

Item (3). By jet prolongation, J^1(A) is Frobenius--Hopf, so the brane tower \{A_n\} is well-defined. Each transition A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} gives a central extension of gerbes banded by the centre \mathcal{B} = Z(\mathrm{Aut}(A_n)). The obstruction class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) exists by the standard gerbe classification theorem, verifying the Quantum lifting condition (quantum lifting).

Item (4). The categorical Euler characteristic equals -6 on Bring's surface by (Bring Euler-characteristic computation).

Item (5). The canonical-system covering \pi \colon \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}(V) has degree 4, genus 4 source, and total ramification R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 14 over exactly 6 branch points by (Riemann--Hurwitz for \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}(V)). \square
